title: file_claim reads the observed value itself; the claimant no longer supplies it
description: Coordinator finding on T-466 after its verdict: file_claim takes observed_value and source from the caller, so a claimant makes a false claim pass the gap check by typing any other value. T-436 section 5 specifies that file_claim reads the respondent's commit act AND reads the one named independent source for the observed value. As built, Outcome A protects nothing against a claimant who lies.
acceptance_criteria: Remove observed_value from file_claim and --observed from the CLI. The source is fixed by the parameter, never chosen by the claimant: a table maps each PR-060 clause 1 parameter to the one harness record that observes it (T-436 section 2 lists the candidates: the blackboard record, goal_mode's exit, usage_report's per-run accounting, the run transcript).

Build a reader for every parameter whose observing record already exists in this harness and can be tied to the commit act's own task id; at least one must exist (deadline against the task's own recorded handoff or completion time is the expected first). Find what goal_mode, usage_report and the event log actually record per task before deciding; list what you found.

A parameter with no reader is refused before anything is written, with a message that the harness cannot replay that claim (T-436 section 2: where a breach cannot be stated as a single-task, single-comparison fact, there is no breach). Pinned by a test that hashes acts/ and the event log.

The gap test is per parameter: equality for task, order and engine; observed exceeds committed for budget, deadline and iteration bound. Move the comparison into one small comparator that returns only a boolean and the two values. Update T-466's AST output-shape guard so it still forbids any damages, window, lapse or reputation computation everywhere, and allows ordering comparisons only inside that comparator; keep its planted-violation negative controls.

Tests in a throwaway root: a true gap files exactly one contest act whose reason names the reader and both values; agreement writes nothing; a claimant cannot influence the observed value through any argument.
Edit attest.py and its tests only; precedent.py belongs to T-474. Do not edit claude.md. Suite passes via goal_mode. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note: plan: investigated what goal_mode/usage_report/events.jsonl/blackboard record per task (reported in handoff). Removing observed_value/source from file_claim; building PARAMETER_READERS table (deadline+iteration_bound via events.jsonl, budget+engine via usage_report.py per-unit singleton-task match); task/order get no reader (no single-task independent source exists), refused with 'cannot replay'. One _gap comparator holds all ordering; extending OutputShapeGuard.

HANDOFF -> verifier: HANDOFF -> verifier. EXPECTED vs ACTUAL below; replay commands included.

WHAT THIS HARNESS ACTUALLY RECORDS PER TASK (investigated before designing readers, per
acceptance criterion 2):
- blackboard task records: claimed_by/claim_expires_at (lease), priority, handoff{from,
  to_role,note,ts}, completed_at/completed_by. attest.py must NOT import the board
  (declare_intent's own existing docstring states this); so readers use events.jsonl,
  never blackboard.json/blackboard.py directly.
- events.jsonl (the real .harness/logs/events.jsonl when root is live, else
  <root>/events.jsonl for a throwaway root -- the same w.is_live(root) split _emit
  already uses): task_claimed{task,holder,lease_seconds}, task_updated{task,status},
  task_handoff{task,from_agent,to_role}, goal_mode_start/goal_reached/goal_abandoned
  {task,cmd,iterations_used,max_iters,duration_seconds}. All carry a clock-stamped ts.
  Measured: most historical goal_mode.py invocations on this board were called with NO
  --task at all (logged as task:"none"), so the iteration_bound reader is frequently
  unable to resolve a value for a real task id, not just occasionally.
- usage_report.py: ties tokens to tasks by regex-matching T-\d{3} in a unit's (one
  subagent transcript's) opening prompt, producing a SET of tasks per unit and ONE raw
  token total (in+out+cache_write+cache_read) for the WHOLE unit -- no per-task split
  when a unit mentions more than one task. Same shape for engine (the unit's model list).
  So budget/engine are single-task facts only for units whose task-mention list is a
  singleton; anything else is not replayable, by construction.
- goal_mode.py: writes no per-task budget, only iterations_used/max_iters keyed by
  (task, cmd) via the persistent .harness/logs/goal_mode_state.json counter AND an event
  line per run.

PARAMETER_READERS TABLE BUILT (attest.py, PR-060 clause 1's six):
  deadline         -> events.jsonl task_handoff / task_updated(status=done), ts
  iteration_bound  -> events.jsonl goal_reached/goal_abandoned, iterations_used
  budget           -> usage_report.py per-unit raw tokens, singleton-task units only
  engine           -> usage_report.py per-unit model(s) mapped to family, singleton-task
                      units only, refused if more than one family
  task, order      -> NO READER. T-436 section 2 names an independent source for the
                      other four explicitly and names none for these two; nothing found
                      in this investigation observes "which task"/"in what order" as a
                      single-task fact independent of the commit act itself, and "order"
                      is inherently a cross-task relation (the exact aggregation section
                      2 refuses to call a breach). A claim against either is refused
                      before any write, message names "cannot replay".

DEFECT CLOSED (coordinator's T-466 finding): file_claim(root, accuser, key_path,
target_name, target_seq, task=None) -- observed_value/source removed entirely, from both
the Python signature and the CLI (--observed-value/--source gone). The source is now
fixed by PARAMETER_READERS, keyed by the parameter the RESPONDENT's own commit act
names, read against that commit act's OWN task id (never a caller-supplied task).
Comparator `_gap(parameter, committed_value, observed_value) -> (bool, committed,
observed)` is the only function with a legitimate ordering comparison; equality for
task/order/engine, observed-exceeds-committed for budget/deadline/iteration_bound
(matching T-436 section 2's own examples, never the reverse direction -- finishing early
or under budget is not a breach). WINDOWS_NOT_RATIFIED unchanged (decision 3's three
numbers still unratified; nothing computes them).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA WALKTHROUGH:
1. observed_value/--observed removed; PARAMETER_READERS table maps 4 of 6 parameters to
   their one reader; table + reasoning in its own docstring in attest.py.
2. Readers built for deadline (first, as instructed), iteration_bound, budget, engine --
   each tied to the respondent's own commit act's task field. Investigation findings
   above.
3. task/order refused before any write with "the harness cannot replay" language;
   NoReaderIsRefusedBeforeAnythingIsWritten class hashes acts/+events.jsonl before/after.
4. _gap is the one comparator (equality: task/order/engine; observed>committed: budget/
   deadline/iteration_bound). OutputShapeGuard extended: READER_FUNCTIONS set asserted
   clean of ordering comparisons, COMPARATOR_FUNCTION (_gap) asserted to contain one
   (positive control), both prior negative controls kept plus a new one planting a
   violation into _read_budget.
5. FileClaimOutcomeA/B, BudgetReaderAmbiguity, EngineReader, DeadlineReader,
   IterationBoundReader, FileClaimCannotBeInfluenced all run in throwaway tempfile roots.
6. Only .harness/bin/attest.py and .harness/tests/test_attest_contracts.py touched
   (git diff --stat confirms); CLAUDE.md untouched; precedent.py untouched (T-474's).
